items.title: Meta-model was XGBoost (boosting), a named deviation from AFML's explicit bagging preference
items.status: CODE_MIGRATED_ALL_141_EDGES_ARTIFACT_REGENERATION_PENDING
items.resolution: AFML SS6.6 (p.100-101): 'It could be argued that in financial applications bagging is generally preferable to boosting... because of the low signal-to-noise ratio.' Blueprint SS4.6 had already flagged Quantara's XGBoost choice as an explicit deviation from this stated preference (P1, 'requires stronger overfit controls'). Concrete motivating evidence found this session: re-scoring US500/volatilitycarry_long's and BTCUSD/absorption_long's historical rows with the saved final (100%-data-refit) XGBoost model produced raw-probability distributions shifted ~0.15 (mean) below their own OOF (CPCV) estimate -- large enough to push the entire calibrated-probability distribution under the OOF-selected deployment threshold, i.e. the deployed model would rarely or never fire despite a seemingly-reasonable OOF-based threshold. Root cause: Step05-09's replay/smoke-test machinery can only re-score historical (= training) data against the final model, which is structurally in-sample for a 100%-data refit -- there is no way, within the old architecture, to distinguish 'this threshold works' from 'this threshold only worked on the model's own training data.' Fix (read directly from the AFML PDF, not a secondhand summary; both source chapters extracted and hand-verified against the book's own worked example before implementation): (1) shared/models/sequential_bootstrap.py implements AFML Ch.4 SS4.5's sequential bootstrap (Snippets 4.3-4.6) -- the book's own 'third and better [best]' solution to bagging under overlapping financial labels -- verified bit-for-bit against a brute-force reference and numerically exact against the book's own SS4.5.3 worked example, then optimized (sqrt-decomposition) for tractability at Quantara's scale (~7x speedup, measured). (2) shared/models/sequential_bootstrap_bagging.py implements AFML Ch.6 Snippet 6.2's clf1 bagging ensemble (DecisionTreeClassifier, criterion=entropy, max_features=sqrt [renamed from removed sklearn 'auto', not a deviation], class_weight=balanced), sequential-bootstrap resampled instead of plain bootstrap, mean-of-probabilities inference (AFML p.94). (3) 02_train_meta_model_optuna.py now follows AFML Ch.9 Snippet 9.1's clfHyperFit two-stage pattern exactly: Optuna tunes a single tree's hyperparameters via the SAME purged CPCV already in place (stage 1, unchanged), then the validated hyperparameters build the bagging ensemble for the deployed final model (stage 2). Optuna itself is not a deviation -- AFML Ch.9 mandates a purged CV underneath hyperparameter search, not a specific search algorithm; Optuna's TPE search is a legitimate, more efficient substitute for the book's own GridSearchCV/RandomizedSearchCV, doing the identical job. (4) 03_generate_oof_predictions.py's CPCV folds now use the SAME bagged-ensemble estimator (not a plain single tree) so OOF predictions come from a structurally identical kind of model to what is actually deployed -- this is the direct fix for the divergence, and is a considered extension of AFML's principles to Quantara's OOF-then-deploy architecture (the book's own clfHyperFit workflow does not have a separate OOF-calibration stage to reconcile). (5) n_estimators is currently 100 (pilot validation value), not yet AFML's own illustrative 1000 (Snippet 6.2) -- the book does not derive 1000 from a formula (its own Figure 6.1 plots variance reduction only over N in [5,30]; its own Snippet 6.1 worked accuracy example uses N=100); Step02 now prints a realized rho_bar (mean pairwise bagged-tree correlation) and projects, via AFML's own SS6.3.1 variance formula V=sigma_bar^2*(rho_bar+(1-rho_bar)/N), how much benefit raising to 1000 would actually give on real data, rather than copying the book's example number. All 141 edges' Step02/Step03 scripts were propagated via patch_backups/_patcher_step_script_rollout.py (same byte-identical-template mechanism already used for the executable-target migration) and verified byte-identical to each other via tests/test_sequential_bootstrap_bagging_sync.py (which also executes the inlined block and re-proves the AFML SS4.5.3 worked example, not just a text-equality check). CODE is migrated everywhere; ARTIFACTS (model.pkl, best_params.json, OOF predictions, manifests) for any edge that already completed Step01-04 under the old XGBoost architecture are now stale relative to the new code and must be regenerated (Step01/02 on Colab, Step03/04 locally) before Step05+ will run against them -- in progress overnight for US500/volatilitycarry_long and BTCUSD/absorption_long specifically; the other 139 edges have not yet had Step01 run at all under either architecture, so there is no stale-artifact exposure for them, only the (already-complete) code migration. ADDENDUM (found during the overnight regeneration runs, both fixed and propagated to all 141 edges before any edge's artifacts were treated as final): (a) joblib.dump'ing a SequentialBootstrapBaggingClassifier instance directly is unpicklable from any other process (Step05-09, EdgeScorer, live scoring) -- Step02 defines the class inline (Colab constraint) so pickle records it as __main__.SequentialBootstrapBaggingClassifier; overriding __module__ on the inline class does NOT fix this either, pickle's save_global does a strict class-identity check. Fixed by persisting a plain portable dict (real DecisionTreeClassifier objects + plain data, not the wrapper instance) and reconstructing the real class in EdgeScorer.load_model(), the one place that already imports the canonical module -- verified with a genuine subprocess-based producer/consumer test (an in-process pickle round trip does not exercise this bug at all), now a permanent regression test (test_model_pkl_survives_genuine_cross_process_load). (b) Optuna's study was not using a seeded sampler, so re-running 02_train_meta_model_optuna.py (e.g. to regenerate an artifact after an unrelated fix, which is exactly what surfaced this) finds a DIFFERENT best_params.json each time, silently orphaning any already-generated Step03/04 output built from the previous run's best_params. Fixed with optuna.samplers.TPESampler(seed=RANDOM_STATE), making the full Step02 search (and therefore Step03's per-fold bagged ensembles, which consume Step02's best_params) deterministic given the same input data -- the same fixed-seed discipline already used everywhere else in this pipeline (RANDOM_STATE=42 for every tree/bagging draw).

items.title: calibrated_probability (CAL_PROB_COL) is a CPCV-fold-averaged research diagnostic, NOT the live-consistent probability -- do not use it for anything meant to reflect live/allocator-facing scoring
items.status: RESOLVED_AND_DOCUMENTED_2026-09-18
items.resolution: shared/calibration/fit_sigmoid_calibrator_and_thresholds.py:98-109 defines two distinct output columns on every calibrated_oof_predictions.csv: CAL_PROB_COL='calibrated_probability' is an AVERAGE across several different per-fold sigmoid calibrator fits from CPCV (cpcv_calibrate_edge) -- per-fold sigmoid coefficients were empirically shown to vary wildly fold-to-fold (e.g. coef ranging 0.03-0.48 across 10 folds on one edge), so this column does not track raw_probability faithfully; it is retained ONLY for the calibration-quality bucket/ECE diagnostics it was designed for (see code comment tagged QUANTARA_V3_LIVE_CONSISTENT_CALIBRATION_ARTIFACT, 2026-09-15). LIVE_CAL_PROB_COL='live_calibrated_probability' is raw_probability passed through the SINGLE final live sigmoid calibrator (fit_final_live_sigmoid's probability_calibrator_sigmoid_side_<side>.json) -- this is what live scoring and the portfolio_allocator's threshold grid actually use (commit d13ecea9, 2026-09-15: 'Updated the calibration to use the final single fit calibration ... reran the 04 script of every promoted edge so that its live_calibrated_probability column can reside in the calibrated_oof_prediction.csv file'). Each edge's own artifacts/thresholds/*_selected_threshold.json declares its own probability_column (currently 'calibrated_probability' for every edge, by design -- that threshold is explicitly an 'edge-default diagnostic/admissibility threshold; allocator 04C owns final representative/live threshold selection', not the live one) -- any downstream consumer MUST read that field dynamically per edge rather than hardcoding a probability column name, so the threshold value and the column it was computed against always stay in the same probability space. This was found and fixed in shared/independence/asset_independence_lab.py (the v3 statistical edge-independence lab, 2026-09-18) which already read probability_column dynamically per edge (verified correct against all 21 currently-deployed edges) and had its PROBABILITY_CANDIDATES fallback list updated to include live_calibrated_probability with an explanatory comment, so a future missing-field fallback does not silently pick the wrong (fold-averaged) column. STANDING RULE GOING FORWARD: any code written for the portfolio_allocator threshold-selection stage (04B/04C) or any other live-facing/allocator-facing consumer MUST use live_calibrated_probability, never calibrated_probability. calibrated_probability may only be used for the CPCV calibration-quality bucket/ECE diagnostics it was built for, or where an edge's own selected_threshold.json artifact explicitly declares it as that artifact's probability_column (the edge-level diagnostic-threshold case, which is intentionally not live-consistent). Do not rediscover this distinction from scratch again -- check this entry first.

items.book: AFML Ch.1 s.1.3.1.6 Portfolio Oversight, p.8-9: cursus honorum = 1 embargo, 2 paper trading, 3 graduation, 4 re-allocation ('re-assessed frequently and automatically... allocation follows a concave function. The initial allocation (at graduation) is small'), 5 decommission; 'it is preferable to release new variations of a strategy and run them in parallel with old versions'.
items.resolution: Edges start at their full allocator weight. A graded shrink (full -> reduced -> off) driven by the same statistic as the decommission rule reduces an edge's allocation when its live results become inconsistent with its certified backtest. No ramp-up, no account-type split.
items.why: Objective is passing the prop challenge fastest without failing. With a few trades per edge per week, a ramp-up keeps size small for most of the challenge (slower pass) while barely reducing failure risk; failure is driven by drawdown from decaying edges, which the shrink side addresses. The holdout (embargo) run supplies pre-live evidence that the ramp-up would otherwise collect.

items.title: Decommission/shrink rule: PSR-based, 5 shrink levels (100/80/60/40/20%), off only at PSR[0] <= 0.05, 30-bet minimum -- the book gives the statistic and the principle, not these numbers
items.status: IMPLEMENTED_2026-10-23; APPLIED AUTOMATICALLY by the execution bot (owner approval 2026-10-23)
items.book: AFML Ch.1 s.1.3.1.6 p.8-9 (allocations become 'gradually smaller' as performance decays; decommission when below expectations long enough that the theory is not backed by evidence); AFML s.14.7.2 p.203 PSR; 0.95 significance p.205-206; AFML p.211 strategy risk on bets actually taken; s.15.4 p.216-218 strategy risk.
items.resolution: portfolio_live/decommission_rule.py + portfolio_live/config/decommission_rule.json. Per edge, on realized bets of the current certified version only (version start + meta-model sha256 in config; a changed model blocks the verdict): PSR[SR*=0] <= 0.05 -> off; else PSR[SR*=SR_backtest] bands >0.25/0.15/0.10/0.05/else -> 100/80/60/40/20%. Verdicts are recomputed on every run and move back up when evidence improves (no ratchet). Benchmark SR_backtest = per-bet Sharpe of meta-approved bets at the live threshold with broker costs (allocator representative trade ledger). Strategy risk (s.15.4) is reported as a diagnostic only. Tests: tests/test_decommission_rule.py. Live: portfolio_execution_bot.build_order_plan -> edge_decommission_allocation() -> decommission_rule.live_allocations() (recomputed at most hourly, last-good verdicts on disk as fallback, fail closed if none); compute_candidate_sizing multiplies target risk by the allocation. Tests: tests/test_decommission_live.py.
items.why: User decisions 2026-10-23. PSR compares live results with a benchmark and gains certainty with the sample; s.15.4 strategy risk measures design fragility (an edge exactly on its backtest scores ~0.45 vs the 0.05 limit) so it cannot detect decay. Five evidence-graded levels give the 'gradual' reduction without killing an edge that only needs time: off requires 95% evidence of losing money, independent of the shrink level.
items.evidence: First run 2026-10-23: all 6 edges insufficient_sample (0-25 bets since the 2026-10-19 deployment of the 2026-10-17 models). Known limits: the benchmark ledger's threshold was selected on the same OOF rows, so SR_backtest is optimistic (shrink errs early); overlapping same-side bets are treated as separate bets (AFML p.196 merging revisited at Ch.14).
items.supersedes: No decommission rule; drift dashboard KS diagnostics only.

items.title: Gate E (embargo / holdout) decision rule: consistency of the holdout with the backtest's own same-length outcomes; the book states the stage but gives no numeric test
items.status: IMPLEMENTED_2026-10-23 (owner decision)
items.book: AFML Ch.1 s.1.3.1.6 p.8 ('If embargoed performance is consistent with backtest results, the strategy is promoted'; the historical path is one of many possible outcomes); s.11.6 p.155 (a backtest is a single path); s.12.4 p.166 (CPCV judges a strategy by the distribution of its outcomes across paths).
items.resolution: shared/research/holdout_replay.py judge: windows of the holdout's span stepped every 7 days through the backtest (allocator representative ledger: meta-approved bets at the live threshold, broker costs, >= 20 bets per window); share_as_bad = fraction of windows with mean R <= holdout mean R. PASS if >= 30 holdout bets and share_as_bad >= 0.05; FAIL if < 0.05; INCONCLUSIVE below 30 bets. PSR[0]/PSR[backtest] reported as diagnostics. Failed edges are removed from config/edge_universe.json; their folders stay untouched. | 2026-11-04 (owner, RECERT): Gate E is a DEPLOYMENT-stage gate (AFML s.1.3.1.6 p.8: the cursus honorum begins 'Once a strategy is deployed'; the embargo is its first stage), run after the allocator on the live threshold -- not an edge-level gate; a FAIL means not deployed and removal from config/edge_universe.json. Runbook Revision 43.
items.why: The first rule (PSR of the holdout vs the multi-year backtest Sharpe) compared 3.5-6.5 months with a 4-year average and treated that average as exact; the backtests themselves had losing stretches of the same length in 12-38% of periods. The owner asked for the book's meaning of 'consistent'.
items.evidence: 2026-10-23 re-judgement on the same holdout (no new look): HK 17.8%, JPN rangestructure 16.3%, GBPJPY 8.0%, XAUUSD rangestructure 19.9% -> PASS; XAUUSD volatilitycarry 0.0% -> FAIL (removed from edge_universe.json); JPN volatilitycarry 3 bets -> INCONCLUSIVE. Report portfolio_live/outputs/gate_e_holdout/gate_e_holdout_20261023T102834Z.json
items.known_limits: Windows overlap (weekly step), so the share is coarse (4 years hold ~8-14 independent windows of 3-6 months). The backtest benchmark is itself optimistic (geometry/threshold chosen on the same data) -- the Deflated Sharpe (Ch.14) and strategy risk (Ch.15) remain to be applied.
items.supersedes: First Gate E rule of 2026-10-23 (PSR[0] and PSR[backtest] > 0.05).

items.resolution: Canonical text docs/mldp/rules/GATE_D_V4_D078.md (v4.1). Cross-fitted calibration: Platt on stacked CPCV paths WITH AFML return-attribution weights (= the D082 live calibrator), 10 purged + embargoed time blocks, b = weighted base rate. D1: F1(meta acting when calibrated P(win) > b) - F1(primary = 2b/(1+b)), unweighted counts, ISO-week block bootstrap 10,000 draws seed 20261104, PASS if 5th pct > 0. D2: d_i = log loss(b) - log loss(calibrated), return-attribution weighted, PASS if mean - 1.645 week-clustered SE > 0. Gate D = D1 AND D2. AUC / MWU, raw and in-sample live-calibrator log loss, Kendall tau reported.

items.why: The month-matched drift test (ours, 2026-11-02) cannot credit monthly-scale effects (T22) and tests the raw trigger's average, which AFML's high-recall primary does not require; pooling + every-asset agreement let other assets veto an asset's own evidence. 35 Gate 0 tests, 2 passes under the old rule.
